Field report, March 2026 (LOCHA programme team). Environmental compliance under the IEE: all 14 facilities were visited with the health care waste checklist. Sharps containers and safety boxes were in place in 12 of 14 facilities; two dispensaries (Nakwamekwi and Napuu) received replacement sharps boxes and a placenta pit was dug at Napuu. Segregated waste bins were distributed to the maternity wings during the visits. No environmental incidents were reported. Branding and marking: the USAID identity was applied to training banners, the CHV training kits and the sign-in sheets used in March; no equipment was delivered in March so no equipment marking was needed. Coordination: the team attended the Turkana County health sector coordination meeting and the sub-county cold chain meeting, and briefed the County Director of Health on the start-up plan. Gender: two female nurse mentors were recruited among the five mentors, and training schedules were set to finish before 3 pm so that women health workers could travel home in daylight.

Field report, April 2026 (LOCHA programme team). Environmental compliance under the IEE: waste management follow-up visits were made to all 14 facilities; sharps boxes were collected and incinerated at Lodwar Sub-County Hospital by the county incinerator team, and placenta pits were checked at the six facilities that conduct deliveries. The flooding washed out one placenta pit at Kalokol, which was rebuilt on higher ground. No other incidents. Branding and marking: USAID marking was applied to the first three equipment kits and to the solar refrigerators delivered; the marking plan approved by the AOR was followed. Coordination: the team attended the County health sector coordination meeting, the nutrition technical working group and the cold chain meeting; flood updates were shared with the county disaster management committee. Gender: transport vouchers were prioritised for women with danger signs during the road closures, and women CHVs formed the majority of the second CHV cohort.

Field report, May 2026 (LOCHA programme team). Environmental compliance under the IEE: waste management checks continued at all 14 facilities; the incinerator team collected and burned sharps waste at Lodwar Sub-County Hospital and Lokichar Health Centre during the nurses' strike so that waste did not accumulate. No incidents. Branding and marking: all four equipment kits delivered in May carried USAID marking and the handover certificates recorded it; radio scripts for the community messages acknowledged USAID. Coordination: weekly calls with the sub-county health management team were held during the strike; the project agreed mobile clinic schedules with the County Director of Health. Gender: mobile antenatal clinics were staffed by women clinical officers where possible, and the KAP survey enumerators were balanced by sex.

Field report, June 2026 (LOCHA programme team). Environmental compliance under the IEE: waste management checks were completed at all 14 facilities; two solar refrigerators that failed were repaired and the failed batteries were returned to the supplier for recycling rather than discarded. No incidents. Branding and marking: USAID marking was applied to the repaired refrigerators and to the four new kits delivered in June; one health worker training banner was replaced after weather damage. Coordination: the team briefed the Sub-County Commander on the security situation near Lorugum and agreed an escort for outreach; the county cold chain officer joined the repair planning. Gender: women attendants accompanied the outreach teams for deliveries and family planning counselling, and the maternal death notification was reported through the MPDSR channel with no identifying details recorded.

Field report, July 2026 (LOCHA programme team). Environmental compliance under the IEE: waste management checks continued at all 14 facilities; the CMAM sites received segregated bins for RUTF packaging and the county collected the packaging. No incidents. Branding and marking: USAID marking was applied to the MUAC tapes and referral slips printed in July and to the two final equipment kits. Coordination: the project took part in the county nutrition cluster response to the drought, and the county health management team asked the CHVs' screening data to be shared in the weekly drought bulletin. Gender: screening days at water points were timed to avoid the hours women collect water, and mothers with infants were seen first.

Field report, August 2026 (LOCHA programme team). Environmental compliance under the IEE: the final waste management audit covered all 14 facilities; all sharps containers were in place and the placenta pits were in good condition; the project's waste management checklist was handed to the sub-county public health officers. No incidents during the activity. Branding and marking: a final marking audit of equipment, the 14 solar and kit installations and training materials found all items marked; the audit sheet is held with the handover certificates. Coordination: the final handover meeting was held with the County Executive Committee Member for Health, the Director of Health, the sub-county health management teams and the USAID AOR. Gender: women made up most CHVs and most people reached with health education; the handover tools include the sex-disaggregated registers.
